items.action: Patch Outlook first — the exploited zero-day needs only a crafted message in the Preview Pane — then Exchange, SharePoint and domain controllers.
items.details: Also prioritize Exchange Server RCE CVE-2026-118207 (8.8), SharePoint elevation of privilege CVE-2026-120002 (9.9), Outlook RCE CVE-2026-110043 (8.8), Windows Search RCE CVE-2026-116928 (9.8) and Windows LDAP RCE CVE-2026-119958. Twenty of the fixes are Outlook RCEs.
items.summary: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes 1,093 vulnerabilities, 63 rated Critical, including one actively exploited Outlook zero-day (CVE-2026-124194, CVSS 6.5) that leaks NTLMv2 hashes via a crafted email.
items.title: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday: exploited Outlook zero-day steals NTLM hashes

items.action: Apply SAP Notes 3778530, 3778556, 3798345 and 3849308 immediately; treat internet-facing NetWeaver as exposed until patched.
items.details: Patches released November 10, 2026 (SAP Notes 3778530, 3778556, 3798345, 3849308). No active exploitation confirmed as of Nov 12, but a proof-of-concept for the SAML2 bypass (CVE-2026-120017) has been posted publicly and Onapsis delivered a working ICM2SHELL exploit to SAP under coordinated disclosure.
items.summary: SAP's November Patch Day shipped four maximum-severity NetWeaver flaws — ICM2SHELL (CVE-2026-76964, CVE-2026-89126), PROXYGATE (CVE-2026-89103) and a SAML2 authentication bypass (CVE-2026-120017) — all unauthenticated, all allowing OS command execution.
items.title: Four CVSS 10.0 SAP NetWeaver flaws need no login — patch now

items.action: Update every DSM branch to its fixed build; no workaround exists, so patching is the only fix.
items.details: Also fixed: an rsync authentication bypass (CVE-2026-85101, 8.6), three 8.8 flaws in SSOAuth, the Sharing API and the Auth API, an OTP bypass and a VPN API command injection. Fixed builds: DSM 7.4.1-90080-1, 7.3.2-86009-5, 7.2.2-72806-10 and 7.2.1-69057-13. Synology says no workarounds exist — patching is the only remediation. No exploitation confirmed as of Nov 13.
items.summary: Synology's Nov 10 advisories (SA-26:19, SA-26:18) fix 27 DiskStation Manager vulnerabilities, led by CVE-2026-76954 — a pre-authentication SQL injection in the Auth API (CVSS 9.8) that lets unauthenticated attackers read or write arbitrary files.
items.title: Synology DSM patches 27 flaws, including pre-auth SQL injection (CVSS 9.8)

items.action: Treat as unverified leak-site claims for now; affected-sector peers should watch for extortion and phishing using the named organisations.
items.details: Incransom runs a double-extortion model — data is exfiltrated before encryption. The specific data stolen from each victim has not been independently verified, and Tanner Clinic has not published a notice about the incident.
items.summary: The Incransom ransomware group listed three victims on Nov 12: Computacenter subsidiaries Pivot Technology Solutions and Sigma Solutions (US technology), Tanner Clinic (Utah healthcare provider, attack estimated Oct 28, patient data threatened) and the HELP Foundation (Ohio disability-services provider, attack estimated Nov 9).
items.title: Incransom lists Computacenter units, Tanner Clinic and HELP Foundation in one day

items.action: Treat as unverified leak-site claims; watch for follow-on extortion and phishing in the affected sectors.
items.details: Thegentlemen is a prolific ransomware-as-a-service operation active since mid-2025, with over 1,000 victims listed. The specific data stolen from these three victims has not been independently verified.
items.summary: The Thegentlemen ransomware group listed three victims on its leak site on Nov 12: Sielke (German paper and home-goods company), Clancy Systems International (Colorado parking-technology firm, attack estimated Nov 11) and United Pharmacy (Saudi Arabia, breach Nov 11).
items.title: Thegentlemen lists Sielke, Clancy Systems and United Pharmacy on Nov 12

items.action: Treat as an unverified claim; energy-sector peers should watch for related extortion activity.
items.details: The claim has not been independently verified and Franc-Oil has not publicly commented. Leak-site listings are claims by the attackers, not confirmations.
items.summary: The Vexy ransomware group listed Franc-Oil, a Nigerian energy company, on its leak site on Nov 12. The claim was discovered the same evening; no details of the data allegedly taken have been published.
items.title: Vexy ransomware claims Franc-Oil (Nigeria) in Nov 12 leak-site listing

items.action: Financial firms should isolate exposed staging environments, rotate potentially exposed secrets, lock down payment APIs and monitor cloud activity; report fraud via helpline 1930.
items.details: The campaign uses publicly available AI offensive tools (ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI) and has re-attacked victims after incomplete remediation, including on weekends and holidays. The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau convened NBFCs, fintechs and banks on Nov 12 to push API security, VAPTs and real-time fraud detection. CERT-In has not named the operators or a total loss figure.
items.summary: CERT-In's advisory CIAD-2026-0058 (Nov 4) warns that the AI-assisted threat actor 'CRAFTY FALCON' is actively targeting Indian banks, NBFCs, fintechs and payment firms, exploiting weak APIs and exposed staging environments to move funds — often after a Re 1 test transfer.
items.title: CERT-In warns 'CRAFTY FALCON' AI attacks are actively hitting Indian financial firms

items.action: Treat as an unverified leak-site claim; Indian manufacturing peers should check exposure to Incransom tactics.
items.details: Incransom typically follows a double-extortion model, exfiltrating data before encrypting systems. The specific data stolen from Nandan Terry Pvt has not been independently verified.
items.summary: Nandan Terry Pvt, an India-based company, was listed as a victim by the Incransom ransomware group on Nov 12, 2026. India ranks 8th worldwide for ransomware disclosures in the tracking database, with 507 victims recorded.
items.title: Incransom lists Indian firm Nandan Terry Pvt on Nov 12

items.action: Yatra customers should watch for phishing using travel-booking details; treat the claim as unverified until the company confirms.
items.details: The claim has not been independently verified and no details of the data allegedly taken have been published. Yatra is one of India's largest online travel agents.
items.summary: The LockBit5 ransomware group listed yatra.com, the Gurugram-based Indian online travel company, on its leak site; the claim was discovered on Nov 8, with an estimated breach date of Nov 8, 2026.
items.title: LockBit5 claims breach of Indian travel firm Yatra.com
